events.title: Farmers find the first trace of China's terra-cotta army
events.summary: A well near Xi'an leads to the tomb of the first Qin emperor.
events.description: On March 29, 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an, China, found an underground chamber that led to the discovery of the terra-cotta army in the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang: about 8,000 life-size soldiers and horses.
events.notificationBody: In 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an found the first sign of the terra-cotta army.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 29

events.title: Wilhelm Olbers discovers Vesta
events.summary: He finds the brightest asteroid in the sky.
events.description: On March 29, 1807, the German astronomer Wilhelm Olbers discovered the minor planet Vesta, the brightest asteroid in the sky.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 29

events.title: The King and I opens on Broadway
events.summary: Rodgers and Hammerstein's musical makes Yul Brynner a star.
events.description: On March 29, 1951, the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical The King and I debuted on Broadway, making Yul Brynner a star.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 29

events.title: The Twenty-third Amendment is certified
events.summary: Residents of Washington, D.C., gain a vote for president.
events.description: On March 29, 1961, the Twenty-third Amendment to the US Constitution was certified, allowing residents of Washington, D.C., to vote in presidential elections.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 29

events.title: John Tyler is born
events.summary: The 10th US president is born.
events.description: On March 29, 1790, John Tyler, the 10th president of the United States, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 29

events.title: The United States agrees to buy Alaska from Russia
events.summary: William H. Seward negotiates the purchase for $7.2 million.
events.description: On March 30, 1867, the United States agreed to buy Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million, in a purchase negotiated by Secretary of State William H. Seward.
events.notificationBody: In 1867, the US agreed to buy Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 30

events.title: President Ronald Reagan is shot
events.summary: He is seriously wounded two months after taking office.
events.description: On March 30, 1981, US President Ronald Reagan was shot and seriously wounded by John W. Hinckley, Jr., in Washington, D.C., barely two months after his inauguration.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 30

events.title: The Treaty of Paris ends the Crimean War
events.summary: The peace settlement is signed in the French capital.
events.description: On March 30, 1856, the Treaty of Paris was signed, ending the Crimean War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 30

events.title: Vincent van Gogh is born
events.summary: The Dutch Post-Impressionist painter is born.
events.description: On March 30, 1853, the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 30

events.title: Elizabeth, the Queen Mother, dies at 101
events.summary: The former queen consort dies at Windsor Castle.
events.description: On March 30, 2002, Elizabeth, the Queen Mother, queen consort of the United Kingdom from 1936 to 1952, died in her sleep at Windsor Castle at age 101.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 30

events.title: The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris
events.summary: Gustave Eiffel's 300-meter tower is officially opened.
events.description: On March 31, 1889, the 300-meter (984-foot) Eiffel Tower, designed by Gustave Eiffel for the International Exposition of 1889 marking the centenary of the French Revolution, was officially inaugurated in Paris. It opened to the public on May 15.
events.notificationBody: In 1889, the Eiffel Tower was inaugurated in Paris, ahead of that year's world's fair.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 31
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Eiffel Tower

events.title: Matthew Perry signs the Treaty of Kanagawa with Japan
events.summary: The American commodore concludes a treaty with Japan.
events.description: On March 31, 1854, US Commodore Matthew Perry signed the Treaty of Kanagawa in Japan.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 31

events.title: Lyndon B. Johnson announces he will not seek reelection
events.summary: The president ends a speech on Vietnam with a surprise.
events.description: On March 31, 1968, US President Lyndon B. Johnson ended a televised speech about the Vietnam War by announcing that he would not seek reelection.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 31

events.title: Oklahoma! opens on Broadway
events.summary: Rodgers and Hammerstein's first musical debuts.
events.description: On March 31, 1943, Oklahoma!, the first of 11 musicals by composer Richard Rodgers and lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II, debuted on Broadway.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 31

events.title: Rene Descartes is born
events.summary: The French mathematician and philosopher is born.
events.description: On March 31, 1596, the French mathematician, scientist and philosopher Rene Descartes was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 31

events.title: Nunavut becomes a Canadian territory
events.summary: The new territory is carved from the Northwest Territories.
events.description: On April 1, 1999, Canada's Northwest Territories were divided to create Nunavut, whose name means 'Our Land' in Inuktitut. Its capital is Iqaluit.
events.notificationBody: In 1999, Nunavut was created from the eastern Northwest Territories.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 1
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Nunavut

events.title: Apple Computer is founded
events.summary: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne form the company.
events.description: On April 1, 1976, Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne formed Apple Computer Inc.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 1

events.title: The Royal Air Force is formed
events.summary: Britain creates an independent air force during World War I.
events.description: On April 1, 1918, the United Kingdom's Royal Air Force was formed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 1

events.title: The Netherlands grants equal marriage rights to same-sex couples
events.summary: It is the first country to do so.
events.description: On April 1, 2001, the Netherlands became the first country to grant equal marriage rights to same-sex couples.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 1

events.title: US troops land on Okinawa
events.summary: The landing begins the Battle of Okinawa.
events.description: On April 1, 1945, US troops landed on the Japanese island of Okinawa, beginning the Battle of Okinawa in World War II.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 1

events.title: Argentine troops seize the Falkland Islands
events.summary: The invasion starts the Falkland Islands War with Britain.
events.description: On April 2, 1982, Argentine troops seized the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas), starting the Falkland Islands War with Britain.
events.notificationBody: In 1982, Argentine troops seized the Falkland Islands, starting a war with Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 2

events.title: Pope John Paul II dies
events.summary: The pope since 1978 dies in Vatican City.
events.description: On April 2, 2005, Pope John Paul II, bishop of Rome and head of the Roman Catholic Church since 1978, died in Vatican City.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 2

events.title: Woodrow Wilson asks Congress to declare war on Germany
events.summary: The president seeks US entry into World War I.
events.description: On April 2, 1917, US President Woodrow Wilson asked Congress for a declaration of war against Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 2

events.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey premieres
events.summary: Stanley Kubrick's film opens in Washington, D.C.
events.description: On April 2, 1968, Stanley Kubrick's film 2001: A Space Odyssey had its world premiere in Washington, D.C.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 2

events.title: Confederate troops evacuate Richmond
events.summary: The Confederate capital is abandoned.
events.description: On April 2, 1865, Confederate troops evacuated Richmond, Virginia, the capital of the Confederate States of America.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 2

events.title: The Pony Express begins carrying mail
events.summary: Relay riders link Missouri and California.
events.description: On April 3, 1860, the Pony Express began delivering mail by horse relay between St. Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California, a route of nearly 2,000 miles covered in about 10 days.
events.notificationBody: In 1860, the Pony Express began relaying mail between Missouri and California.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 3
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Pony Express

events.title: The first handheld mobile phone call is made
events.summary: A Motorola employee calls Bell Laboratories.
events.description: On April 3, 1973, the first handheld mobile telephone call was made by an employee of Motorola, who called AT&T's Bell Laboratories.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 3

events.title: Martin Luther King, Jr., gives his Mountaintop speech
events.summary: He speaks in support of striking Memphis sanitation workers.
events.description: On April 3, 1968, Martin Luther King, Jr., delivered his 'I've Been to the Mountaintop' speech in Memphis, Tennessee, at an event for the city's striking sanitation workers.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 3

events.title: Harry Truman signs the Marshall Plan into law
events.summary: The program aims to revive Europe's economies after World War II.
events.description: On April 3, 1948, US President Harry S. Truman signed into law George C. Marshall's plan to revive the economies of western and southern Europe after World War II.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 3

events.title: Outlaw Jesse James is shot dead
events.summary: Robert Ford kills him at his home.
events.description: On April 3, 1882, the American outlaw Jesse James was shot and killed by Robert Ford at his home.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 3

events.title: Martin Luther King, Jr., is assassinated in Memphis
events.summary: The civil rights leader is shot while standing on a balcony.
events.description: On April 4, 1968, the civil rights leader Martin Luther King, Jr., was shot and killed while standing on a balcony in Memphis, Tennessee.
events.notificationTitle: A civil rights leader is killed
events.notificationBody: In 1968, Martin Luther King, Jr., was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 4

events.title: Twelve countries sign the North Atlantic Treaty
events.summary: The treaty creates NATO.
events.description: On April 4, 1949, twelve countries signed the North Atlantic Treaty, forming the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 4

events.title: Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft
events.summary: The company becomes the largest maker of PC software.
events.description: On April 4, 1975, Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft, which became the world's largest personal-computer software company.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 4

events.title: William Henry Harrison dies after a month in office
events.summary: He is the first US president to die in office.
events.description: On April 4, 1841, US President William Henry Harrison died of pneumonia one month after taking office, the first US president to die in office.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 4

events.title: Maya Angelou is born in St. Louis
events.summary: The author of I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings is born.
events.description: On April 4, 1928, Maya Angelou, the poet and author of I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, was born in St. Louis, Missouri.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 4
